neighbours.label: nouns for people or activities that perform for an audience (singers, athletes, football, performing arts)
fire: The workshop teaches the breathing skills that dancers need to stay healthy.
Many young gymnasts suffer from wrist injuries during training.
The hall seats around two hundred musicians and guests.
This diet plan was designed for professional athletes in heavy training.
The coach worked hard to change the style of football the team played.
A perfect warm-up for actors before they go on stage.
She bought tickets for the ballet at the new performing arts centre.
The choir is looking for more singers for the spring concert.
quiet: The workshop teaches the breathing skills that nurses need to stay healthy.
Many young cashiers suffer from wrist injuries during training.
The hall seats around two hundred students and guests.
This diet plan was designed for office workers in a busy season.
The manager worked hard to change the style of management the firm used.
A perfect warm-up for drivers before they go on the road.
She bought tickets for the train at the new central station.
The library is looking for more volunteers for the spring sale.

notes: Card: peaks on ' Football' x4, ' athletes' x2, ' football' x2, ' performing' x2, ' singers'. The list suggests a shared pattern: performers and performance fields. Tested on new performer nouns (dancers, gymnasts, musicians, actors); near misses swap in non-performing groups of people in the same slot.
